page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the n4 family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance processing capabilities in the average tier. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is recorded at 1672.09, while the multi-core performance reaches 7217.53. Geekbench scores align with this, showing a single-core score of 1877.0 and a multi-core score of 7215.0. The CPU features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which support workloads like image processing with a Geekbench score of 6439.0 and ray tracing with a Geekbench score of 9855.0.

A key tradeoff is the memory subsystem performance. While cached small-block read bandwidth is high at 568.81 GB/sec, the PassMark memory score is weak, falling into the bottom 25% at 1718.22. Large-block uncached read and write speeds are 68.85 GB/sec and 40.33 GB/sec respectively. Additionally, LLM text generation for medium 7B models is weak at 7.92 tokens/sec, though prompt processing for the same model achieves 52.37 tokens/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high-density compute-to-RAM ratio, making it suitable for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage.

This instance is configured for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, static web serving, and basic machine learning inference on small models. The Geekbench clang software compilation score is 8701.0, and static web serving throughput is measured at 11.89 GB/sec. It is also suitable for multi-threaded decompression tasks, as demonstrated by a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 37.58 GB/sec.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel processor with 4 physical cores and dedicated CPU allocation. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks generally fall within the average range, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7215.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12045.57. However, memory performance is a notable tradeoff, with a PassMark memory score in the bottom 25%. Supported by Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, the instance is suited for CPU-intensive tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, and small-scale machine learning inference, where a low 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio is acceptable.
